issues.description: Method 'acceptSupplyDelivery' has inconsistent parameter lists across artifacts. The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md line 30) and textual description (problem_statement.md lines 72-73) describe acceptSupplyDelivery as acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — i.e., four parameters including a supplier name. The provided template example in Main (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 20) calls acceptSupplyDelivery with three arguments (shop.acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100)), and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 47) defines public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch (four vs three parameters, and presence/absence of a supplierName parameter) will confuse students about the required method signature and which parameters they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across problem statement, template/example, and solution. Two valid options: (A) Update the problem statement UML and descriptive text to the three-parameter form acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and document that supplier information is not required; or (B) Change the template/example and solution to include the supplier parameter (acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) and update all example calls accordingly. Apply the chosen change to the UML, the textual description, all example call sites in Main.java, and the SealSaloon implementation so students see a single, consistent API to implement.
